name: Open Items
rows: Fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 · cash at June 30, 2026 · operating account ending 4471 and payroll account ending 6158 at Cinderbrook Bank
DRAFT FOR THE CPA · audit procedures · not an audit report · no opinion

The bank’s 12 monthly charges on the payroll account ending 6158, $4,065.00 for FY2026, were never recorded. Payroll cash is overstated and expenses understated by $4,065.00. Proposed adjustment: debit a bank charges expense, credit 1020 payroll cash. It is under the $17,000.00 clearly trivial, so it is listed and not added up; the CPA may pass it. The bank feed should post the charges each month. The machine never posts.

Check 21561, $21,850.80, to Sound Waste & Recycling Co. for invoice SWR-2511-1294 of December 18, 2025, has never been presented and was 194 days old at June 30, past the bank’s 180-day limit. The vendor has not been paid, yet the books count the invoice as paid. Ask the Controller to contact the vendor and reissue it or void it with a stop payment. If voided: debit 1010 operating cash, credit 2000 accounts payable (or an unclaimed property liability). Above clearly trivial; a classification with no effect on income.

The bank confirmed $5,723,107.14; the request showed the books’ $5,534,665.71. The $188,441.43 difference is explained in full: 8 checks that cleared July 1 to 7 ($170,655.63), plus check 21561 ($21,850.80), less the payroll account charges ($4,065.00). No adjustment beyond FEE-01 and STALE-01. The CPA accepts the explanation or asks for more.

Both June 30 reconciliations were prepared by Marisol Zielinski, Project Accountant, on July 12, 2026 and foot, but neither is signed as reviewed: the control walkthroughs’ REC-01 (CLS-2). The charges sat on the payroll reconciliation all year and the December check went unfollowed. Recommendation: the Controller signs each reconciliation within 15 days and follows up any item older than 60 days.

All of the company’s cash, $5,723,107.14 per the bank, is at one bank, Cinderbrook Bank; $5,473,107.14 is above the FDIC’s $250,000.00 insurance. The draft notes have no concentration of credit risk note. Disclosure is a judgment for the CPA. No cash is restricted, pledged or held back, and the loans require no compensating balance.

The bank confirms interest accrued June 1 to 30, 2026 of $17,040.00 (term loan ending 2208) and $11,625.00 (line ending 3315), paid through May 31 and debited July 1. The books record interest when debited: the liabilities search’s UL-04 and the covenant procedures’ INT-01. Not counted again here.
Materiality is proposed at $340,000.00, 0.5% of revenue; performance materiality $255,000.00; clearly trivial $17,000.00. The engagement partner sets it.
These are draft workpapers and a draft findings memo for the engagement partner. They are not an audit report and give no opinion. Nothing has been posted, signed or sent to the client or the bank.
